guarantees.claim: When err_rsp_pending is 1 and tl_h_i.d_ready is asserted, err_rsp_pending is cleared to 0 on the next cycle; the captured fields retain their values.

When err_rsp_pending is not in the clearing condition (i.e., not (err_rsp_pending && tl_h_i.d_ready)) and a new TL-UL request is accepted (tl_h_i.a_valid && tl_h_o_int.a_ready), err_rsp_pending is set to 1 and err_source, err_opcode, err_size, err_instr_type are updated with the request's fields on the next cycle.

assumptions.risk: If a_valid is asserted for a non-error transaction, the module will capture invalid opcode/size/instr_type and later drive a malformed error response on the D channel, possibly violating TL-UL protocol or leaking internal state.

assumptions.claim: When err_rsp_pending is set to 1, the downstream consumer will eventually assert tl_h_i.d_ready to accept the pending error response, ensuring progress and avoiding deadlock.
assumptions.risk: If d_ready never asserts, err_rsp_pending stays high forever, blocking capture of any future error response; error handling stalls.

assumptions.cond: when a new error response needs to be captured
assumptions.risk: If a_ready is permanently low, no new error request can be captured, causing loss of error information and stalling error reporting.

uncertain_points.claim: When both err_rsp_pending && tl_h_i.d_ready and tl_h_i.a_valid && tl_h_o_int.a_ready are true in the same cycle, the clearing branch takes precedence, so the new request is not captured. Is dropping a simultaneous new error request the intended behavior, or should it be buffered?
uncertain_points.risk: If a new error occurs exactly when the previous error response is accepted, that error is silently lost, which could be a safety/security concern if the second error is critical.

uncertain_points.claim: If err_rsp_pending is high and tl_h_i.d_ready is low while a new valid request arrives (tl_h_i.a_valid && tl_h_o_int.a_ready), the new request is not captured because the set condition is not taken (due to else-if). This means only one error response can be pending at a time; any error arriving before the first is cleared is silently discarded.
uncertain_points.risk: Multiple back-to-back errors are collapsed, potentially losing crucial fault information needed for diagnostics or security response.
